title: SCOPE: Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise LLM Judging
claim: A reliable judge pipeline: score both orderings into an entropy uncertainty signal, then calibrate a threshold that bounds error among accepted outputs.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, chevrons between, worked numeric example flowing top-down
description: Three rounded panels read left to right, linked by grey chevrons: 1. Pairwise Judging, 2. BPE Uncertainty, 3. SCOPE. Panel 1 stacks a task box, a user question ("Explain why the sky looks blue"), a green Assistant A box and a red Assistant B box, a blue LLM judge box with a small neural-net icon, and an example verdict [[A]] with a doubt note. Panel 2 runs top-down through forward pass (p_fwd=0.95), reverse swapped pass (p_rev=0.85), aggregation (p̄=0.90), and an entropy score with a green-to-red gradient bar marking s=0.33 and the formula worked out. Panel 3 starts with the target risk α=0.10, then conformal calibration (maximize λ s.t. risk ≤ α), an inference check on a gradient bar with s=0.33 against λ̂=0.41, and a green Decision: Accept box. Pastel pill labels and vertical arrows guide the eye.
caption: Overview of the SCOPE framework. (1) Pairwise judging: for a user query q and two candidate responses (rA, rB), the LLM judge returns a single preference token. This raw verdict is sensitive to the order in which the two responses are presented. (2) Bidirectional Preference Entropy (BPE): to neutralize potential position bias, the pair is scored in both orders. The forward pass gives pfwd = Pθ(y=A | xfwd) and the reverse pass gives prev = Pθ(y=B | xrev), since preferring rA corresponds to label A in the forward order and label B in the reverse order. The two are averaged into a bias-neutral preference ¯p = (pfwd + prev)/2, and its binary entropy s(x) = −[¯p ln ¯p + (1 −¯p) ln(1 −¯p)] (in nats, maximized at ¯p=0.5 with value ln 2 ≈0.69) is the uncertainty score: small s(x) reflects a confident, order-stable preference, whereas large s(x) reflects ambivalence or disagreement across orders. (3) SCOPE: the user specifies a target risk α (e.g., 0.10), the largest acceptable error rate among accepted judgments. Conformal calibration on a labeled set returns the largest threshold ˆλ certified to keep this error within α. At test time, the judgment is accepted when s(x) ≤ˆλ and is abstained otherwise.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as scalable judges in pairwise evaluation, but they remain prone to miscalibration and biases. We propose \textsc{Scope} (Selective Conformal Optimized Pairwise Evaluation), a framework that calibrates an acceptance threshold so that, under exchangeability, the error rate among non-abstained judgments is at most a user-specified level $Î±$. To supply \textsc{Scope} with a bias-neutral uncertainty signal, we introduce Bidirectional Preference Entropy (BPE), which queries the judge under both response positions and converts the order-averaged preference probability into an entropy-based score. Across various pairwise judging benchmarks, BPE outperforms standard confidence proxies in calibration and discrimination, while \textsc{Scope} consistently satisfies the target risk bound (empirical FDR $\approx 0.097$--$0.099$ at $Î±=0.10$) and retains substantial coverage. Compared to vanilla baselines, \textsc{Scope} accepts up to $2.4\times$ more judgments under the same risk constraint, demonstrating that BPE enables reliable and high-coverage LLM-based evaluation.
